q: 1. The tricalcium aluminate in cement has the property of
options: generating large amount of heat of hydration
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts very rapidly with water, is largely responsible for the initial setting behaviour of cement, and generates a large amount of heat of hydration — all of these properties apply.

q: 2. If the engineer-in-charge approves, the 10 cm cubes may be used for the work test of concrete provided maximum nominal size of aggregate, does not exceed
explain: As per code provisions, smaller 10 cm cubes can be used instead of standard 15 cm cubes only when the maximum nominal size of the aggregate does not exceed 20 mm, with engineer's approval.

q: 3. High percentage of tricalcium silicate and low percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: A cement rich in C3S and low in C2S hardens rapidly, develops high early strength, and generates high heat of hydration — all these characteristics occur together.

q: 4. Cement used for normal concrete construction, is obtained by burning a mixture of
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured by burning a mixture containing siliceous, argillaceous, and calcareous raw materials together to form clinker.

q: 5. Low percentage of tricalcium silicate and high percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: Cement low in C3S and high in C2S hydrates slowly with low heat generation and low early strength (though good ultimate strength) — so none of the listed rapid/early/high-heat effects apply.

q: 6. The cement whose strength is a little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength, is known as
explain: Low-heat Portland cement gains strength more slowly in the early months due to reduced C3S/C3A content, but eventually catches up to match the strength of ordinary cement.

q: 7. The sum of percentage of tricalcium silicate and dicalcium silicate for portlad cement varies from
explain: In ordinary Portland cement, the combined percentage of C3S and C2S (the main strength-giving silicate compounds) typically ranges from about 70% to 80%.

q: 8. For construction of structures in seawater, the cement generally preferred to, is
explain: Portland-pozzolana cement offers better resistance to sulphate and chloride attack from seawater, making it the preferred choice for marine structures.

q: 9. The cement widely used in retaining wall is
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is the most commonly and widely used cement for general structures including retaining walls, as per this text.

q: 10. Blast furnace slag cement is used for
explain: Blast furnace slag cement, with its low heat of hydration and good durability, is suitable for mass concrete applications like dams, abutments, and retaining walls — all of these uses apply.

q: 11. The cement becomes useless if its absorbed moisture content exceeds
explain: When cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, premature hydration and lump formation occur, rendering the cement useless for construction.

q: 12. Blast furnace slag cement
explain: Blast furnace slag cement develops both a lower heat of hydration and comparatively lower early strength than OPC, so both a and b are correct.

q: 13. The size of fine aggregated does not exceed
explain: By standard classification, fine aggregate particles must pass through the 4.75mm IS sieve, so their size does not exceed 4.75mm.

q: 14. Concrete gains strength due to
options: chemical reaction of cement with sans and coarse aggregates
explain: The chemical hydration reaction between cement and water forms the cementitious gel that binds the aggregates together, which is the fundamental source of concrete's strength.

q: 15. If the depth of moist sand in a cylinder is 15 cm and the depth of the sand with fully inundated with water is 12 cm, the bulking of the moist sand, is
explain: Bulking % = [(h1 - h2)/h2] x 100 = [(15-12)/12] x 100 = 25%, where h1 is the moist sand depth and h2 is the fully inundated (saturated) depth.

q: 16. The quality of cement is tested by
explain: Compressive strength testing of standard mortar cubes is the primary and most common method used to assess and certify the quality of cement.

q: 17. Low heat cement is used in
explain: Low heat cement is specifically used in thick/mass concrete structures, where controlling the heat of hydration is essential to prevent thermal cracking.

q: 18. If X, Y, Z are the fineness moduli of coarse, fine and combined aggregates, the percentage (P) of fine aggregate to combined aggregates, is
explain: The formula for the percentage of fine aggregate needed to achieve a combined fineness modulus, based on the fineness moduli of coarse (X), fine (Y), and combined (Z) aggregates, is p = [(X-Z)/(Z-Y)] x 100.

q: 19. The method of voids for determination of quantity of cement paste assumes that
options: voids in coarse aggregates are filled by fine aggregates
voids in fine aggregates are filled by the cement paste
volume of fine aggregates is equal to total voids in coarse aggregate plus 10% extra
volume of cement paste required is equal to total volume of voids in fine aggregates plus 15% extra
explain: The voids method of proportioning is based on sequentially filling voids: fine aggregate fills coarse aggregate voids (plus extra), and cement paste fills fine aggregate voids (plus extra) - all these assumptions together form the complete method.

q: 20. The diameter of needle used in Vicat's apparatus for the determination of initial setting time is prescribed as
explain: The Vicat needle used specifically for the initial setting time test has a prescribed diameter of 1mm as per standard specifications.

q: 21. Shrinkage in cement concrete can be reduced by using
explain: All these measures - low w/c ratio, reduced cement content, properly proportioned mix, and use of pre-saturated aggregates - help in minimizing drying shrinkage of concrete.

q: 22. In a cement store, the size of cement pile is 4 m × 3 m and its height is 1.8 m. The number of cement bags in the pile could be
explain: Using standard warehouse assumptions (about 0.3m² floor area and 0.18m height per bag), the volume of the pile (4×3×1.8 = 21.6m³) accommodates approximately 400 bags of cement.

q: 23. Shrinkage in cement concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Shrinkage of concrete is primarily caused by the loss of water from the cement paste, so it is directly proportional to the water content present in the mix.

q: 24. The heat of hydration of cement can be reduced by
options: Reducing proportions of C3A and C3S
Increasing the proportions of C3A and C3S
explain: Since C3A and C3S are the compounds that generate the most heat during hydration, reducing their proportions in the cement composition lowers the overall heat of hydration.

q: 25. Shrinkage in cement concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Since shrinkage originates in the cement paste (not the aggregates), a higher cement content in the mix directly increases the overall shrinkage of the concrete.

q: 26. Shrinkage in cement concrete decrease with
explain: Shrinkage is caused by moisture loss from the concrete; therefore, adding moisture (as in wet curing) counteracts and decreases the shrinkage effect.

q: 27. Vicat's apparatus is used for
explain: The Vicat apparatus (with the standard plunger) is primarily used to determine the standard/normal consistency of cement paste.

q: 28. Increase in fineness modulus of aggregate indicates
explain: A higher fineness modulus value indicates that the aggregate contains a larger proportion of coarser particles, i.e., coarser grading.

q: 29. The diameter of the vicat plunger is 10 mm and its length varies from
explain: As per IS specifications, the Vicat plunger, 10 mm in diameter, has a length that varies within the range of about 40 mm to 50 mm.

q: 30. Soundness test of cement by Le-Chatelier's apparatus gives unsoundness due to
explain: The Le Chatelier soundness test primarily detects unsoundness caused by excess free (uncombined) lime in the cement.

q: 31. Weight of an oven dry sand and air dry sand are 500 gm and 520 gm respectively. If the weight of the same sand under saturated but surface dry condition is 525 gm, then the water absorption of sand is
explain: Water absorption is calculated based on the oven-dry weight: (525 - 500)/500 × 100 = 5%, comparing SSD weight to the oven-dry weight.

q: 32. Maximum shrinkage takes place in cement concrete after drying for
explain: Drying shrinkage continues over an extended period, with the maximum shrinkage generally being observed after about one year of drying.

q: 33. Maximum permissible limit of magnesia content in OPC is
explain: As per IS 269 specifications, the maximum permissible magnesium oxide (magnesia) content in OPC is limited to 6%.

q: 34. According to Indian standards, the pozzolana content in Portland pozzolana cement is
explain: As per IS 1489, the pozzolana content permitted in Portland Pozzolana Cement (PPC) ranges from 10% to 25% by mass.

q: 35. Soundness test of cement by Le-Chatelier's apparatus gives unsoundness due to
explain: The standard Le-Chatelier apparatus test specifically detects unsoundness caused by free (uncombined) lime present in the cement.

q: 36. Poisson's ratio for concrete ranges between
explain: The typical Poisson's ratio for concrete lies within the range of 0.11 to 0.21, depending on the mix and testing conditions.

q: 37. As compared to static tests the dynamic tests on concrete give
explain: Dynamic (vibration-based) testing methods generally yield a higher value of Poisson's ratio for concrete compared to static (load-based) testing methods.

q: 38. For ordinary cement, the maximum expansion by Le Chatelier method should not be more than
explain: As per IS specifications, the maximum permissible expansion for ordinary Portland cement measured by the Le-Chatelier method should not exceed 10mm.

q: 39. For 1 bag of cement (50kg) the quantity of water required is
explain: Using a typical water-cement ratio of about 0.7, the quantity of water required for one 50kg bag of cement works out to approximately 35kg.

q: 40. In the manufacture of pozzolana cement, the amount of pozzolana material added to ordinary Portland cement clinker is about
explain: As given in this text, about 30% pozzolanic material is blended with OPC clinker in the manufacture of pozzolana cement.

q: 41. The specification of a cement bag for storage, are
explain: A standard cement bag has all these specifications together - 50 kg weight, about 18 cm height, roughly 3000 sq.cm plan area, and about 35 litres volume.

q: 42. The degree of grinding of cement is called
explain: Fineness of cement refers directly to the degree to which the clinker has been ground into fine powder.

q: 43. Ware house pack of cement means
options: pressure exertion of the bags of upper layers
pressure compaction of bags on lower layers
explain: 'Warehouse pack' refers to the compaction/packing effect experienced by the lower bags due to the pressure exerted by the weight of bags stacked above them.

q: 44. The hardening is the phenomenon by virtue of which
options: the cement doesn't undergo large change in volume when treated with water
the plastic cement paste changes into hard mass
the cement paste sets and develops strength
explain: Hardening specifically refers to the process by which the plastic cement paste, after setting, transforms into a hard, rigid mass over time.

q: 45. Ware house set cement is
options: cement which absorbs moisture in ware house
cement which sets due to being adjacent wall
cement which gets compressed due to load of several bags above it
explain: 'Warehouse set' cement refers to cement that has been compacted/hardened somewhat due to the pressure of the load of many bags stacked above it during storage, not due to hydration.

q: 46. The phenomenon by virtue of which the cement doesn't undergo large change in volume when treated with water is known as
explain: Soundness is defined as the property of cement to not undergo significant volume change (expansion) after setting when reacted with water.

q: 47. Light weight concrete is used for
explain: Due to its lower density and reduced structural strength, light weight concrete is mainly suitable for non-load bearing walls and partitions.

q: 48. If the effective plan area of a warehouse is 54sq.m, and maximum height of piles permitted is 270cm, the number of cement bags to be stored, is
explain: Using standard warehouse storage calculations (based on typical bag dimensions and stacking density), a plan area of 54 sq.m with a pile height of 2.70 m works out to approximately 2700 bags of cement that can be stored.

q: 49. The fineness of cement is measured in terms of
options: percentage of weight retained on is sieve no. 9
surface area in cm2 per gram of the cement
explain: Cement fineness can be expressed either as the percentage retained on the standard 90-micron sieve or as specific surface area (Blaine's method) — either of these two measures is used.

q: 50. An air-entraining agent when added to cement improves
explain: Air-entraining agents introduce fine air bubbles that act as lubricants between particles, primarily improving the workability of the concrete.
